record_notes.DCP-LETT-1847: April 2, supplied 1856; all three body blocks and three notes read. Invitation offers April 23 or 26 around the Hookers, with Wollaston and Watson uncertain. Private chair upstairs is Darwin reporting Emma, not a separate Emma letter. Coach time contains genuine MathML three and a quarter, not raw 314. Preserve the stated thirteen miles to Farnborough and two to Down without modern correction. Abstract received and seen; cover missing. Later diary evidence of actual visitors does not turn proposed dates into completed attendance. No bibliography section.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1852: April 9, supplied 1856; all six blocks and three notes read. Replies to missing Huxley acceptance/health news and acknowledges lecture card. Visit planned for April 26, train time 3 o 15 minutes and dinner seven; the train notation is not MathML. Lecture card does not prove attendance on April 22. No bibliography section.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1868: May 4, supplied 1856; all seven blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Reports 117 pounds advanced to Sowerby over two or three years for Ray Society work and asks council intervention; anticipated bankruptcy is a concern, not an established event. P6 newly acknowledges Chinese Pots note received this minute on May 4, which cannot activate earlier main-body writing. That incoming note is missing. Later 1857 repayment and outstanding balance are apparatus, not current knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1878: May 27, supplied 1856; all three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Notes to Overstone and Lubbock already written but to be posted tomorrow, so dispatch remains prospective. Lecture arrived this morning but not yet read; probable third lecture identification is editorial, not a certain source identity. Prior receipt of the first two lectures is separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1914: July 1, supplied 1856; all ten blocks, ten notes and bibliography read. Asks about bipolar ascidians with explicit tropical sampling caution, not a completed universal distribution. Proposed catalogue not assumed finished. Eternal-hermaphrodite phrase is physiological argument, not an identity instruction. Last lecture read; missing current antenna question receives detailed explanation of position, cement and dissection. Future root-earth observations, permission to keep slides and offer to send antennae remain distinct. Later quoted Huxley Boltenia caution does not reconstruct a missing incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1922: July 8, supplied 1856; all three blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Thanks a missing Huxley letter and conditionally uses cautious Boltenia information. Returns an unreadable word for clarification, asking for its return; surviving incoming not established. Polyzoa receptacle, ova and hermaphroditism remain questions with uncertainty. Later book quotation supplies a witness, not the missing full letter. Earlier 1914 is another Darwin letter and cannot be the prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2017: December 9, supplied 1856; all eight blocks, fourteen notes and bibliography read. Missing Huxley note reports Siebold facts about unfertilised eggs and affects Darwin doubts concerning neuters. Forwarding the note to Lubbock is a plan, not completed dispatch. Book not yet borrowed/read; 1857 translation is later. Cement receptacle/ovarian continuity defended against homology objections; Conchoderma dissection proposed. Later 1859 Krohn correction is not current knowledge. Birth December 6 and non-attendance at club are personal news; December 11 discussion is still future. Preserve source Hicks with apparatus Hincks distinction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2020: December 13, supplied December 1856; all eight blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Excluded salute node actually contains dateline 13th, so date must not be discarded as greeting. Thanks missing Huxley note; translation reading and Conchoderma dissection remain prospective. Pellets in ovarian tubes are reported observation, whereas Italian bee species status is attributed contemporary opinion. P6–8 are a separate set of questions about hermaphroditism, organ transitions and correlated characters, not an existing answer or modern asserted truth. Historical notebook instruction is content only. Earlier 1757 is Darwin outgoing, not a candidate incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2037: January 4, supplied 1857; all four blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Congratulates Noel birth and replies to missing Huxley note. Identifies Balanus as balanoides and says it does not live beneath lowest tide. Bringing specimens to London is planned, not already delivered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2041: January 17, supplied 1857; all four blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Darwin heard only part of the January 15 Huxley/Tyndall lecture and left with headache. Questions whether fracture and regelation permit force transmission and flow, as distinct from mere wet-glass coherence, especially below freezing. Gun-barrel sand, screw and wood analogies are hypothetical, not performed experiments. Does not replace gravity as force by a new claim; apparatus distinguishes gravity from communication of force. Missing Huxley response is not this outgoing letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2045: February 3, supplied 1857; all three blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing Huxley answer to glacier questions, seeks Tyndall experiment in severe frost and hopes it has already been done without claiming it was. Owen dispute is reported personal news. Same-author 2041 cannot be an incoming prompt. Later apparatus says research did not directly address Darwin below-freezing question.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2118: July 5, supplied 1857; all five blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Asks Huxley to read two enclosed manuscript pages, linked editorially to four fair-copy folios, about Brulle/Barneoud and Milne Edwards. Full enclosure is not inline here; partial apparatus quotations cannot supply the whole prompt. Goodsir paper read with admiration but explicit inability to judge independently; elephant/tapir vertebra inference questioned. Lecture and Mysis development acknowledged; bat embryology is a separate question. Huxley July 7 response supports a scoped reverse link to the embryological query.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2119: July 7, 1857 ALS, seven manuscript pages; all twelve retained blocks, nine notes, full three-part French enclosure, separate Darwin annotations and bibliography read. Huxley distinguishes Brulle factual errors from logical insufficiency and appearance time from duration of development. His observations on Mysis, Rathke Astacus and simple ophthalmic peduncles refute the alleged complexity sequence; fish/mammal brain and heart comparison is another test. Milne Edwards characteristic is distinguished from most complex, with chorda dorsalis and house analogy. Botanical verdict is a suspicion, not observation of plants. Preserve raw of of duplication and French conseacute;quent artifact pending supported repair. The numbered French quotations are Brulle as copied with acknowledged errors by Huxley, not Huxley endorsed theory. Darwin scored/crossed notes are undated separate hands. No actual figure assets.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2122: July 9, supplied 1857; all seven blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Thanks the July 7 analysis, concedes unsafe evidence and posterior-development blunder, and withdraws the Brulle discussion. Retains a conditional Barneoud analogy to Milne Edwards in P3–4 and interpretation of perfect and important in P6. These concessions are not wholesale abandonment of species theory. Scientific-man heart-of-stone phrase is original prose. P7 Allman fertilisation report is new separate material, not evidence Huxley supplied it. Draft plan/type variant belongs to apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2141: September 15, supplied 1857; all four blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Three lectures now read and forwarded to Lubbock, unlike the prospective forwarding in 2017. Praises classificatory account despite cirripede difficulty; nerve detail new to Darwin. Belief Huxley still on holiday remains in source even though editorial evidence reports earlier return. Do not forward instruction is historical address content.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2143: September 26, supplied 1857; all eight blocks, fourteen notes and bibliography read. Replies to missing Huxley critique of Agassiz, glaciers and cockroach anatomy. Darwin read Westwood to locate other authors; no claim he has read each cited Serres, Audouin, Brulle or Hummel work. Book/organ details remain uncertain, Hummel via Westwood. P7 introduces genealogical classification and analogy/homology distinction; future ability to draw pedigrees is hypothetical, not an achieved classification. Next Huxley 2144 is a separate demonstrable response for the next packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1668: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. April 18 with supplied 1855 year. Forwards missing Bell opinion, asks recipient to read and burn: historical quoted instruction does not authorize any file deletion. Acknowledges Lindley higher claim but uncertain about alternating biological subfields; weighs Hancock/Westwood and quotes Huxley opinion to Bell. Has written Bell but meeting and final award decisions still future. Huxley note on Lyell separate missing input. Reports De la Beche death. Later rule history and medal outcomes are editorial evidence, not assumptions about current settled procedure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1697: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Explicit accepted batch-15 primary full reading reused with matching source pins. June 10 with supplied 1855 year. Independently read additional witness in full. Asks Huxley to speak for Barrande and Dana at next council if Darwin cannot attend, explicitly enclosing an old Lyell note; footnote identifies April 23 source 1672 and shared dual candidature plus Barrande primordial work confirms it. Conditional request not to answer if attending does not prove attendance. Huxley lecture abstract has been read with disappointment; exact title identity is apparatus and missing cover note remains missing. Upcoming marriage congratulations are not proof wedding already occurred. Later June 14 and July 21 events separate. This source is not a reply to Lyell but uses his incoming evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1759: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Day 3 with September 1855 supplied from related drawing chronology. Huxley drawings received and annotated; no separate surviving cover-note text. Actual two preserved images viewed: stalked Lepas anatomy with cement-gland arrow, ovarian branching, oesophagus/stomach and peduncle-muscle directions; sessile Balanus drawing with pencil cross and sub-oesophageal-ganglion placement direction. These combine Huxley imagery and Darwin corrections; cannot use amended image as pristine incoming prompt or turn editorially typeset image captions into invented original prose. Body distinguishes unseen Lepas cement gland from probable position by analogy, and asks ganglion, stomach, antenna and testes changes. No proof original physical ink/pencil layers can be isolated from these reproductions. Later printed revised drawings in 1857 remain future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1757: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Day 29 with September 1855 supplied from recent Huxley marriage and autumn reference; later than September 3 source 1759 despite lower ID. Missing Huxley anatomical letter provoked detailed response, not a surviving Darwin outgoing substituted as prompt. Darwin admits weak microscopy, distinguishes observed ducts and cellular appearances from interpretation as true ovaria, defends repeated connections while accepting that gut-formed gland relation may differ. Own failure to see cement gland in Lepas remains explicit, contrasted with other genera. Leonard artist drawing recalled is not itself reproduced here. Footnote 3 loosely associates gut-formed gland with cement gland, while body explicitly refuses that identity; retain source-layer distinction. P1 includes see P.S. cross-reference. In P7 he newly retrieves, examines and breaks up preserved specimen, finding pulpy matter and no cell with included nuclei/granules in that specimen, while maintaining he saw cells in others. Do not flatten this later examination into pre-existing observation in P1–6 or global retraction of all observations. Later Huxley 1857 lecture, Krohn 1859 criticism and modern Crisp analysis remain apparatus, not a preserved incoming prompt or Darwin present knowledge.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Viewed actual stalked cirripede section: appendages and elongated peduncle, left cement-gland arrow/cross near top of peduncle; typeset directions on branching ovarian tubes/caeca, oesophagus bell shape/stomach breadth and transverse/oblique peduncle muscles. Source reproduction mixes drawing, marks and editorially typeset annotation, not pure incoming diagram.

Viewed actual sessile cirripede cutaway: concentric shell/body boundaries, appendages and internal looping structures. Cross near central-right loop accompanies typeset instruction to move main sub-oesophageal ganglion left. No unannotated precursor image can be recovered from this reproduction.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
